vail-co: Big and lively. Packed base-village decks in Vail Village and Lionshead, with live music and pricey cocktails.
beaver-creek-co: Polished and quiet. Fireside drinks in the plaza, and warm chocolate-chip cookies handed out at 3pm.
breckenridge-co: Rowdy and easy to find. A real Main Street full of bars and breweries a short walk from the lifts.
keystone-co: Family-first. River Run's village has a few relaxed bars and fire pits; most people head home early.
aspen-snowmass-co: Glamorous in Aspen, with champagne at Ajax Tavern and the Cloud Nine party scene. Snowmass is calmer.
steamboat-co: Western and friendly. Base-area bars on the plaza, and a real cowboy downtown with saloons and live music.
telluride-co: A historic mining town reached by free gondola. Old saloons on Main Street, plus pricier spots in Mountain Village.
crested-butte-co: Funky and local. Elk Avenue's old-town bars are the place; the base area is quiet.
winter-park-co: Casual. Base-village bars and a lot of Front Range day-trippers heading home by sundown.
arapahoe-basin-co: Tailgates. 'The Beach' parking-lot row of grills and coolers, plus the 6th Alley Bar in the base lodge.
wolf-creek-co: Basically none. Food in the day lodge, then a drive to Pagosa Springs for the hot springs.
park-city-ut: The busiest in Utah. Historic Main Street has dozens of bars, and High West Saloon is right off the Town Lift.
deer-valley-ut: Refined. Fireside drinks in the lodges and the Sticky Wicket at Silver Lake; Park City's Main Street is close.
alta-ut: Low-key and lodge-based. The Goldminer's Daughter saloon at the Wildcat base, the 1939 Sitzmark bar at Alta Lodge, and shot skis at the Peruvian.
snowbird-ut: Lively for a canyon resort. Cheap shots and beers at the Tram Club, and the Cliff Lodge's top-floor bar.
solitude-ut: Quiet. A small village with a pub or two; most people drive back down the canyon.
powder-mountain-ut: Very little by design. A lodge drink, then down the hill to Eden or Ogden.
snowbasin-ut: Grand day lodges with fireplaces and drinks, but no town. Ogden's bars are 30 minutes away.
jackson-hole-wy: Legendary. The Mangy Moose for live music in Teton Village, and the Million Dollar Cowboy Bar's saddle seats in town.
grand-targhee-wy: Small and mellow. The Trap Bar in the base village is the whole scene, and it's a good one.
big-sky-mt: Spread out. A few base-area bars, plus ranch-style saloons a drive away. Plan around distances.
whitefish-mt: Fun and unpretentious. The Bierstube and Hellroaring Saloon on the mountain, then a real western town below.
bridger-bowl-mt: A non-profit local hill. Lodge beers, then Bozeman's bars and breweries 25 minutes away.
sun-valley-id: Old-Hollywood classic. The Sun Valley Lodge's bars and the saloons of Ketchum, which has a proper town.
schweitzer-id: Small village bars with lake views, then the town of Sandpoint down the road.
taos-nm: European-flavored. A few bars in the small base village; the town of Taos has adobe bars and New Mexican food.
palisades-tahoe-ca: Busy village scene. The 'Chammy' (Le Chamois & Loft Bar) is the classic, with sunny decks all spring.
heavenly-ca: The rowdiest in Tahoe. Casinos and nightclubs at the state line, a short walk from the gondola.
kirkwood-ca: Remote and quiet. A couple of base bars; no town nearby, so it's mostly lodgers.
mammoth-mountain-ca: Big and spread out. Canyon Lodge and the Village have bars, and the town has plenty of breweries.
mt-bachelor-or: Lodge beers only on the mountain. Bend, 30 minutes away, has one of the best brewery scenes in the country.
timberline-or: Historic and quiet. The Blue Ox Bar inside the 1937 Timberline Lodge is the move.
crystal-mountain-wa: Modest. A couple of base-area bars; no town, so most people drive back to Seattle.
stevens-pass-wa: Day-trip feel. Lodge bars, then Leavenworth's Bavarian-themed town 40 minutes east.
mt-baker-wa: Almost none. Lodge beers, then the road back to Glacier or Bellingham.
stowe-vt: Classic New England. Spruce Peak's village and the bars and restaurants along the Mountain Road into town.
killington-vt: The East's party mountain. The Access Road is lined with bars and late-night clubs like the Wobbly Barn.
sugarbush-vt: Retro and friendly. Wünderbar at the base, plus the Mad River Valley's taverns.
jay-peak-vt: Remote and family-heavy. A few resort bars and the indoor waterpark; not much of a town.
stratton-vt: Lively village. Grizzly's at the base has live music most weekends.
okemo-vt: Family-focused. A handful of base bars, then the small town of Ludlow.
sunday-river-me: Two bases with bars, and a few classic spots on the access road. Bethel is a small town nearby.
sugarloaf-me: Remote and loyal. The Bag & Kettle in the village is a Maine institution.
loon-mountain-nh: Easygoing. Base-lodge bars, then the small town of Lincoln.
whistler-blackcomb-bc: World-class. A huge pedestrian village with packed patios, from the GLC to dance clubs late at night.
revelstoke-bc: Small base village, then a genuine railway town with good brewpubs. Low-key, not a party scene.
big-white-bc: Ski-in village with a few pubs and a family crowd. Kelowna is an hour away.
sun-peaks-bc: A compact, walkable village with a handful of pubs and patios. Friendly, quiet nights.
fernie-bc: A real mountain town. The Griz Bar at the base, then historic downtown Fernie's pubs.
lake-louise-ab: Lodge bars at the base, then mostly back to Banff, which has a busy bar scene 40 minutes away.
banff-sunshine-ab: The Mad Trapper's Saloon in an old log lodge up top, then the bars of Banff town.
kicking-horse-bc: Small base village with a couple of bars. Golden has a few pubs; it's a skier's town.
panorama-bc: Hot pools and a small village of bars. Relaxed and family-friendly.
mont-tremblant-qc: Lively and European-feeling. A colorful pedestrian village with bars, music and poutine.
alyeska-ak: Small but fun. The Sitzmark bar at the base and the Girdwood town scene; the hotel has a spa too.
lutsen-mn: North Shore cozy. Charlie's Alpine Bistro (rebuilt Papa Charlie's) and live music at the Lofty Gondola bar.
giants-ridge-mn: Iron Range easy. The Burnt Onion chalet and lodge bars; Biwabik is a small Bavarian-style town.
afton-alps-mn: Day-hill casual. Paul's Pub in the chalet has a full bar and a double-sided fireplace.
buck-hill-mn: A suburban hill. Food in the chalet and a quick drive home.
welch-village-mn: Small and friendly. The Black Diamond Bar in the main chalet and Madd Jaxx in the east chalet.
wild-mountain-mn: Day-hill casual. Food in the chalet; Taylors Falls is down the road.
andes-tower-hills-mn: Family hill. Food in the chalet; Alexandria's lake country is nearby.
mount-bohemia-mi: Wild. A Nordic spa with hot pools and saunas at the base, a log cabin bar, a tiki bar and a rooftop bar.
big-powderhorn-mi: Old-school UP. Lodge food, plus trailside 'wine huts' you can rent for the day.
whitecap-mountains-wi: Remote Northwoods feel. Food in the lodge; not much else nearby.
powder-ridge-ct: A small day hill. Food in the lodge and a quick drive home.
red-lodge-mt: Day lodge on the hill, then a real western town with historic bars six miles down.
loveland-co: None to speak of. Lodge beers, then the drive back to Denver or Georgetown.
indianhead-mi: Midwest casual. Lodge food at Snowriver's Indianhead base, and small UP towns nearby.
blackjack-mi: Midwest casual. Lodge food at Snowriver's Blackjack base.
copper-mountain-co: Moderate. Center Village has a handful of bars and patios; it quiets down by evening.
